svg.title: Rapamycin (sirolimus): what has actually been tested
svg.desc: Rapamycin (sirolimus): what has actually been tested. Approved medical use: Kidney-transplant rejection prevention and LAM (FDA, since 1999); boxed warning. Verdict: Approved. Lifespan in mice: NIA testing program: longer life at three sites, in both sexes (2009, 2014). Verdict: Strong in mice. Lifespan or healthspan in dogs: One 10-week pilot in 24 dogs; the large TRIAD trial is under way. Verdict: Under way. Lifespan in people: No human trial has tested whether it extends life. Verdict: Not tested. Aging measures in healthy adults: Small or short trials (6 to 129 people); mostly surrogate measures, mixed. Verdict: Preliminary. Immune aging (related drugs): Better vaccine response, fewer infections in phase 2; phase 3 missed. Verdict: Mixed. Safety: Infections, mouth sores, higher lipids and glucose, slow healing, red-cell drops. Verdict: Known risks.
